'''J'oopi Shé''' was a [[Force-sensitive]] [[Kadas'sa'Nikto]] from the [[planet]] [[Kintan]] who became a [[Jedi Master]] in the [[Technical division]] of the [[Jedi Order]], the guardians of the [[Galactic Republic]]. He was stationed in the [[Imperial Palace|Jedi Temple]] on the planet [[Coruscant]]<ref name="CVD" /> and in [[19 BBY]]<ref name="Galactic Atlas">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas: Updated Edition]]'' dates the events of {{Film|III}} to [[19 BBY]].</ref> attended a briefing given by [[Jedi]] Master [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] in one of the building's [[Jedi Temple communication center|conference rooms]].<ref name="ROTS">{{Film|III}}</ref>

The briefing was on the [[Outer Rim Sieges]] being conducted by the Republic as part of the ongoing [[Clone Wars]] against the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]]. After the meeting concluded, Shé left the conference room while in conversation with<ref name="ROTS" /> [[Jedi Knight]] [[Melik Galerha]]<ref name="Visual Encyclopedia" /> as Jedi Knight [[Anakin Skywalker]] rushed past them to enter the room.<ref name="ROTS" /> Shé had [[Color|blue]] [[eye]]s<ref name="Visual Encyclopedia" /> and scaly gray-green skin. The [[Nikto]] wore brown [[Jedi apparel|Jedi robes]], including brown [[boot]]s and a brown [[utility belt]] where he hung his [[lightsaber]].<ref name="CVD" />

==Behind the scenes==
J'oopi Shé appeared in the [[prequel trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']],<ref name="ROTS" /> which was released on [[May 19]], [[2005]].<ref name="YbY">''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, New Edition]]''</ref> In the current ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]], he was identified in the [[2017]] reference book ''[[Star Wars: The Visual Encyclopedia]]''.<ref name="Visual Encyclopedia" /> The name originated in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, where it was first used in the deluxe edition of the reference book ''[[Dressing a Galaxy: The Costumes of Star Wars]]'', which was written by [[Trisha Biggar]]<ref name="Dressing">''[[Dressing a Galaxy: The Costumes of Star Wars]]'' {{C|Deluxe Edition}}</ref> and published on [[October 11]], 2005.<ref name="DressingDate">{{WebCite|url=https://www.waterstones.com/book/dressing-a-galaxy-part-1/trisha-biggar/george-lucas/9780810959644|text=Dressing a Galaxy: Part 1: The Costumes of Star Wars (Hardback)|work=[[Wikipedia:Waterstones|Waterstones]]|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/mxQvt|archivedate=2022-04-24}}</ref>
